channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Strike date set: SFUSD teachers to walk off jobs Monday
item.description: The city’s 50,000 public school students are in limbo as negotiations between district and union remain stuck.

item.title: The Sunset’s new food destination is a snack shack with a wild streak
item.description: Ruby’s brings smashburger tacos and fisherman’s stew to Ocean Beach.

item.title: Inside the final days of Jonathan Kuminga’s doom-loop Warriors tenure
item.description: Wednesday’s trade with the Atlanta Hawks delivered the 23-year-old wing his long-standing wish of a fresh start elsewhere.

item.title: Fluted and looted: A prized instrument goes missing in the Tenderloin
item.description: A jazz musician says she stored $20,000 in belongings — including a flute she’d played for 35 years — in her new apartment. A day later, all was gone.

item.title: Super Bowl celeb stalking: Everywhere in SF we’ve seen famous people so far
item.description: A running catalogue of A- to D-list visitors and where they’re hanging in the days leading up to the big game.

item.title: How ‘the skies parted’ for Super Bowl QB Sam Darnold as a 49er
item.description: Advice from Jerry Rice, encouragement from Frank Gore, and coaching from Kyle Shanahan helped transform the Seattle signal-caller’s career.

item.title: The Castro Theatre reopens Friday: We got a first peek inside
item.description: After a controversial two-year renovation, SF’s soaring movie palace returns in all its glory.

item.title: Jeffrey Epstein’s hidden ties to San Francisco’s Museum of Modern Art
item.description: Justice Department documents show Epstein donated a co-owned piece and supported other work.

item.title: SF political group dropping nearly $2 million to support moderates
item.description: The amount puts the group in the upper echelons of spending in local races.

item.title: With strike looming, SF parents’ loyalties are with teachers — for now
item.description: “Whatever they are asking for, I am completely 100% behind them,” said one Clarendon Elementary School mom.
